design_reference: Editeur Livre-Jeu - Wireframes.dc.html § 04 → 4D « MONSTRE · création à la volée »: identity (NOM + visuel deferred), CARACTÉRISTIQUES (PV / ATTAQUE / DÉFENSE), outcome reveal texts, BUTIN LÂCHÉ (loot via shared ObjectEditor), « Ajouter à la librairie du générateur » (reusable across books). Combat outcomes resolve to réussite/échec — the only semantic colours (green/red), per § 05. Mounted via node-editor's « Action requise » seam. Low-fi wireframe.

plan.goal: Let an author configure a node's « Monstre » action — the monster's name and the player-facing reveal text for each combat outcome (réussite / échec) — mounted via the ActionRegistry, with a stub to save the monster to a reusable library.
acceptance_criteria: action-monster self-registers a « Monstre » editor with the brain ActionRegistry; node-editor's « Action requise » control offers « Monstre » alongside « Décor »/« PNJ » with zero node-editor changes (Open/Closed, KR-051).
Selecting « Monstre » mounts the editor for that node; structural screens (sommaire/mort) never show it.
The editor captures the monster name + a player-facing reveal text for EACH of the two outcomes; both are persisted on the node via BookService.

The two outcomes are réussite and échec — the only semantic outcomes — rendered with the only semantic colours (réussite = good/green, échec = bad/red), derived from the brain ROLL_OUTCOMES registry (KR-117), never hardcoded or branched on.

A « Ajouter à la librairie du générateur » affordance emits monster:savedToLibrary{bookId,nodeId} on the brain event bus (library stub; the reusable-monster catalog + persistence is a later iteration).

All monster config is persisted through BookService.updateNode (no private copy, KR-020) and lives on the node document; action-monster and node-editor never import each other (wired at the composition root).

The editor renders strictly from design-system primitives/tokens (Field, Badge good/bad), light theme; controls are keyboard-operable with ≥44px targets and the outcome fields carry an accessible name.
plan.walking_skeleton: registerActionMonster registers an ActionEditor { type:'monstre', label:'Monstre', render } with the brain ActionRegistry (wired at the App composition root). MonsterEditor reads node.monster live via useOpenBook and writes via BookService.updateNode: a NAME Field, and for each RollOutcome from the brain ROLL_OUTCOMES registry a good/bad Badge + a reveal-text Field. « Ajouter à la librairie » emits monster:savedToLibrary. Stats (PV/Attaque/Défense), loot, combat-reinforced-by-object, outcome targets, and the real library are later iterations.

iterations.goal: Combat mechanics (§ 4D): PV / Attaque / Défense stats; outcome targets (victoire → poursuit / fuite → reliaison) wired through edges; defeat → Mort (the automatic combat path, KR-067).
Loot (« butin lâché ») via the shared ObjectEditor + combat reinforced by an inventory object (« si le joueur possède … alors victoire automatique »).
Reusable monster library via a MonsterLibraryService (« créer / librairie du générateur », reusable across books), consumed from the monster:savedToLibrary event.

known_risks: KR-050/051 — node-editor is a host: action-monster self-registers via the ActionRegistry and is mounted without being imported; adding the action needs zero node-editor changes.

KR-091 — combat/skill outcomes are réussite/échec ONLY, the only semantic colours; their label + tone live in the brain ROLL_OUTCOMES registry (KR-117) and the editor derives both outcomes from it — never hardcode « Réussite »/« Échec » or branch on the value. ROLL_OUTCOMES sits in brain because trap/skill-roll editors will reuse it (KR-109).
KR-020 — monster config is read/written through BookService (the SSOT); the editor holds no private copy and reflects live via useOpenBook.
KR-090 — monster config lives on the node document (node.monster); structural screens never carry it (updateNode's text-only guard for sommaire/mort, KR-055).
KR-013 — derive the editor's current values inline from the live node, not via a useEffect-synced mirror.
monster:savedToLibrary is wired as a contract now but has no consumer/persistence yet (library stub) — the real MonsterLibraryService lands in iteration 3, like the deferred Object/PNJ catalogs.

KR-097 — the reusable MONSTER LIBRARY is a persisted CROSS-BOOK store (brain MonsterLibraryService over the raw local store, not synced), distinct from the within-book derived references (KR-062/096): a library monster is INSTANTIATED as an independent COPY (different books can not share a live reference), with node-specific targets stripped on save and a fresh loot id on instantiate (KR-003).

iterations_log.label: walking-skeleton
architecture_choices: Third action-* feature: self-registers with the brain ActionRegistry at the App composition root (registerActionMonster) — the seam now mounts three editors (« Décor »/« PNJ »/« Monstre ») with zero node-editor changes (KR-050/051).

réussite/échec — the only semantic outcomes — modelled as a brain ROLL_OUTCOMES registry (Record<RollOutcome,{label,tone}>, KR-117) placed in brain because trap/skill-roll editors will reuse it (KR-109). MonsterEditor derives BOTH outcome rows from it (good/bad Badge + reveal Field), no hardcoded labels/branches.
MonsterEditor is a VIEW over BookService (KR-020): reads node.monster via useOpenBook, normalised once (DEFAULT_MONSTER + the cleaned pattern), writes via updateNode.

The monster-library is stubbed via a new monster:savedToLibrary event on the brain EventBus (per CLAUDE.md's event list) — wired now, consumed later. Added ariaLabel to the shared Field so the Badge-captioned outcome fields keep an accessible name.
deviations_from_plan: Stats (PV/Attaque/Défense), loot, combat-reinforced-by-object, outcome targets, and the real reusable-monster library are deferred to iterations 1–3; the skeleton ships name + réussite/échec reveal texts + the library-event stub.

test_coverage.integration: action-monster via App — « Monstre » offered through the registry seam, name + both réussite/échec outcome texts persisted, « Ajouter à la librairie » emits monster:savedToLibrary; structural-screen guard now covers monster (BookService)

iterations_log.label: iteration-1
architecture_choices: Combat mechanics: MonsterConfig gained pv/attack/defense stats edited with the shared brain Stepper, plus victoryTarget/fleeTarget node references. A skeleton monster (name + outcomes only) is normalised with stat defaults on read ({ ...DEFAULT_MONSTER, ...node.monster }) so it still loads and canonicalises on write (KR-116).

Two brain extractions at their SECOND consumer (KR-109, same rule as ObjectEditor/OutcomesEditor): the value Stepper (action-pnj gift + action-monster stats) and the TargetPicker (PNJ « mène à » + monster victoire/fuite) moved to brain/components; action-pnj refactored to import them (its feature-local TargetPicker deleted, GiftSection's local ValueStepper removed). TargetPicker gained label/emptyLabel props to stay generic.

Outcome targets follow the established config-reference deferral (like PNJ « mène à » / trap fatal): victoire → « poursuit » and fuite → « reliaison » are node-id references on the config (structural screens excluded, KR-067; dangling surfaced, KR-021/063), pending promotion to rendered edges via the dedicated combat path. Défaite → Mort is the AUTOMATIC combat path (KR-067) — surfaced read-only, never an authored edge / never the manual edge API.

MonsterEditor stays a VIEW over BookService (KR-020); réussite/échec reveal texts still derive from ROLL_OUTCOMES via the shared OutcomesEditor (KR-091/117). The library button still emits the monster:savedToLibrary stub (iteration 3).
deviations_from_plan: « wired through edges » is realised as config references + the automatic defeat→Mort statement, NOT rendered tree edges yet — the dedicated combat-edge path (KR-067) that draws victoire/fuite/défaite on the canvas is deferred, consistent with the PNJ/trap deferrals; the model captures the intent now.

Dangling targets are UI-surfaced in the TargetPicker (⚠ cible supprimée) but NOT yet SSOT-pruned: since targets are config references (not edges), BookService does not drop them on node delete — that pruning lands with the edge promotion (KR-021/063 fully closed then). Pre-commit tech-lead nit: added a NaN guard to the now-shared brain Stepper for parity with clampGiftValue.
Loot + combat-reinforced-by-object (iteration 2) and the reusable MonsterLibraryService (iteration 3) remain deferred.

test_coverage.unit: (shared) Stepper + TargetPicker covered via the pnj/monster integration tests
test_coverage.integration: action-monster via App — PV stepper persists, victoire → poursuit target select (structural screens excluded, KR-067), automatic défaite → Mort statement shown; existing name/outcomes + library-event tests still green

iterations_log.label: iteration-2
architecture_choices: « Butin lâché »: MonsterConfig gained an optional loot (GameObject). A « Le monstre lâche un butin » Toggle reveals the SHARED brain ObjectEditor (its FOURTH consumer after décor/pnj/the gift, KR-052/109) — name internal + player-facing description, stable id minted once via blankLoot/createId (KR-003). Toggle off drops the loot (undefined → dropped by JSON). VIEW over BookService (KR-020), no private copy; written via the canonical patchMonster.

The ObjectEditor is edited live (no modal): a monster's loot has no draft-commit/cancel need (unlike décor's per-row modal where a cancelled NEW object must not land) — the toggle already gates whether loot exists, so live-edit through ObjectEditor is the simpler correct shape.
deviations_from_plan: « Combat reinforced by an inventory object » (« si le joueur possède … → victoire automatique ») is DEFERRED to the ObjectCatalogService work: it is the SAME by-id inventory-object reference as choice-linking's hidden prerequisite (KR-062), which needs the shared object catalog (action-decor iter 3 / choice-linking iter 3). Capturing it by object NAME now would violate KR-062 (references by stable id, never by name), so it pairs with the catalog rather than introducing a by-name reference to untangle later. Loot — the self-contained half — ships now.
Loot is a SINGLE dropped object (toggle + ObjectEditor, mirroring the PNJ gift), not a list; a multi-item butin is a possible refinement.

test_coverage.unit: blankLoot mints a fresh stable id (covered via integration)
test_coverage.integration: action-monster via App — toggling « lâche un butin » reveals the shared ObjectEditor, authoring it persists loot.name + a stable id, toggling off drops the loot

iterations_log.label: iteration-3 (reusable monster library)
architecture_choices: New brain MonsterLibraryService — a PERSISTED, CROSS-BOOK library of reusable monsters (« la librairie du générateur »), wired in createBrain over the RAW local store (not a book document, not cloud-synced) under MONSTER_LIBRARY_KEY. Cache-backed list() for useSyncExternalStore snapshot stability; useMonsterLibrary hook (KR-013).

Unlike the within-book PNJ/object references (resolved LIVE, KR-062/096), a library monster is INSTANTIATED as an independent COPY: different books can not share a live reference, so « Choisir dans la librairie » deep-clones the saved config onto the node with a FRESH loot id (KR-003, so re-uses do not collide) and keeps this node own victory/flee targets (the library config carries none — they are stripped on save).

« Ajouter à la librairie » now actually persists (monsterLibrary.save) in addition to emitting the long-wired monster:savedToLibrary event (it consumes the previously-stubbed event path). A new MonsterLibraryPicker (searchable popover) mirrors the action-decor/pnj reuse pickers.
deviations_from_plan: Cross-device SYNC of the library is out of scope — it persists via the raw local store (per-device), like UIPreferences. The combat-reinforced-by-object hidden-prereq (iter 2 deferral) remains deferred; this slice is the library half.

test_coverage.unit: MonsterLibraryService (save/list/remove, strip targets, snapshot stability, subscribe, survives reload under the dedicated key)
test_coverage.integration: action-monster via App — Ajouter persists to the library + emits the event; Choisir instantiates a saved monster as a copy onto the node

open_questions: Cross-device sync of the monster library (currently per-device local) — a later refinement if a shared library is wanted.
Combat reinforced by an inventory object (iter 2 deferral): the by-id hidden-prereq reference over collectObjects (KR-062), a small follow-up now that collectObjects exists.
